As a risk analyst, the vendor documents specific defenses against AI-generated faces, deepfakes, and camera-injection attacks — named detection capabilities, not just a marketing mention of fraud
As a risk analyst, the platform detects repeat and duplicate identities across verifications — the same face or document resurfacing under different names is flagged automatically
As a risk analyst, selfie checks match the live user to the document portrait with liveness detection — documented defenses against printed photos, screens, and replayed video
As a developer, I can verify identity against authoritative databases without documents — SSN, national registries, or credit-header data — for lower-friction flows where a doc scan is overkill
As an ops lead, I can verify businesses, not just people — registry lookups, UBO identification, and documented KYB flows that chain into KYC on the owners
As a developer, I can enrich verifications with phone, email, and device risk signals — carrier checks, address history, device fingerprint — as additional documented check types

As an ops lead, the platform verifies government IDs from a documented breadth of countries and document types — passports, national IDs, driver licenses, residence permits — with the supported list published
As a developer, verified sessions return the extracted document fields as structured data — name, date of birth, document number, address, expiry — retrievable via the API, not just a pass/fail flag

As an AI-native user, verification outcomes come back structured enough for an agent to decide on — machine-readable check results, risk signals, and failure reasons an automated onboarding flow can branch on

As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the verification pipeline — create sessions, poll outcomes, retrieve extracted data, and trigger re-checks through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials
As a developer, a sandbox lets me exercise every outcome before going live — documented test documents, personas, or magic values that deterministically produce pass, fail, and review results

As a developer, the whole verification lifecycle is drivable through the API — create a session, get its status, retrieve results and captured media, and cancel or redact it — with every step documented
As a developer, verification lifecycle events arrive as signed webhooks — created, processing, verified, requires-input — so my system reacts to outcomes without polling
As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

As a founder, the vendor documents how biometric data is handled lawfully — GDPR bases, US biometric statutes like BIPA, and the consent language my flow needs — so legal review has something to review
As an ops lead, I can control what happens to collected identity data — documented retention windows and a redaction or deletion API that scrubs PII on demand

As a developer, I can launch a complete document-plus-selfie verification with a hosted or drop-in flow — create a session server-side, redirect or embed, and read the result — without building capture UI myself
As a developer, I get native iOS, Android, and web SDKs with guided camera capture — glare, blur, and edge detection coaching the user to a usable document photo on the first try
As an ops lead, I can send a verification to someone with a no-code link or QR code — no engineering ticket to verify a one-off customer, contractor, or seller
As a developer, a person verified once can be recognized and reused across sessions or products — documented re-verification and reuse of a prior passed check instead of forcing a full re-run
As a founder, I can see verification funnel analytics — pass rates, drop-off points, completion time by country and document type — to know what verification is costing me in signups
As an ops lead, borderline verifications land in a manual review queue with the full evidence — document images, extracted fields, check results — and reviewer decisions feed back into the record
As an ops lead, I can configure verification logic without code — conditional steps, risk-based routing, country-specific requirements, and template changes that don't need an engineering deploy
As an ops lead, screening is not one-shot — previously verified users are continuously re-screened against watchlist updates, and changes raise events I can act on
As an ops lead, I can screen verified users against sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media watchlists as part of the same verification — one vendor, one API, one review surface
